doc.title: Roy McCurdy interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995

title: Musicians interchange and West Coast versus New York feel
summary: Players move among groups, and he plays lighter in Los Angeles than in New York.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And you’ve been with Nancy for what, you said sixteen years?
Yeah, about sixteen years now. Long time.

I wish someone could make up a chart about how musicians have moved from one group to the other. I mean you mentioned Bob Cranshaw and he played with Sonny Rollins, and you played with Sonny Rollins, and it gets very complicated, but word gets out who’s good.

Oh, yeah. And everybody moves into the, yeah, it kind of intertwines. Even when you’re playing with local people, if you’re playing out in Los Angeles around local things, people, it seems to be the same musicians playing with different groups all the time. It’s really kind of interchanging all the time.
Is there a difference in, these days, in the feel of jazz on the west coast and in New York?

Oh, yeah, I think so. Music is still played hard here. They did it hard, they play hard, you know there’s a lot of fire. And when I tend to play out there I usually play a little lighter than I would usually. When I come back here, I naturally dig in because it’s the way the guys play back here. I think so, yeah. I think the feeling is a little different. The music is good on both sides, but I think the feeling of playing it is a little bit different.
